[Podcast: Side Door, episode 14. Host: Nina. Guest: the user.]

NINA: So you left a design agency job and now you run operations with AI agents. What actually happened?

GUEST: Honestly it was less brave than it sounds. The agency folded our team in August. I had about six weeks of savings. I started automating the boring parts of my own job search because I couldn't afford to waste hours on it.

NINA: Like what?

GUEST: Sourcing. I wrote a script that pulled job posts, scored them against what I actually wanted, and drafted a first note for each one. It cut my search from something like four hours a day to maybe forty minutes. The drafts were bad, but bad drafts are faster to fix than blank pages.

NINA: Did it work?

GUEST: It got me interviews, not offers, at first. The offers came when I stopped sending the drafts as-is. People can tell. The one thing I'd tell anyone is: automate the search, never automate the voice.

NINA: That's a good line.

GUEST: I stole the shape of it from my old creative director. She used to say "automate the invoice, never the idea."

NINA: What's the Substack about, then?

GUEST: It's the notebook of that switch. What I tried, what broke, what the tools really cost. Last month the stack cost me about eighteen dollars. People assume it's hundreds.

NINA: Where do people find it?

GUEST: Just search my name on Substack. I post Notes most days and one longer piece on Sundays.
